correctness.rationale: In characteristic three, the independent square classes t,t-1,t-lambda,t-mu give a smooth connected degree-16 Galois cover branched simply at five points and of genus five. Exactly five nontrivial characters have four negative inertia values and thus genus-one quotients; the other ten have genus zero. Explicit pullback/norm maps have composite diag[8], with all mixed terms zero by distinct characters, hence a prime-to-three isogeny. The Hasse invariant for Legendre y²=x(x-1)(x-r) is -(1+r), so each shared triple has a unique supersingular fourth point. Distinct four-subsets of a five-set cannot both be supersingular. This proves f=5,a=0 or f=4,a=1. The five explicit divisor equations are equivalent cross-ratio tests, disjoint on the smooth parameter open, and each has q-3 Fq points. Symbolic Groebner saturation gave the unit ideal for all ten divisor pairs, and an independent field enumerator over F9 and F27 reproduced the formula. Finite enumeration is not used as proof of the infinite statement.

Papers restricted to characteristic zero cannot entail those characteristic-three assertions.

originality.rationale: The Humbert–Edge family and elliptic factor decomposition were published, and are explicitly excluded from the new claim. The assessed contribution is the exact characteristic-three p-rank/a-number dichotomy, five disjoint supersingular-component equations, Newton slopes, and a uniform ordered F_(3^m) count. Primary inspected texts concern complex quotient classification or general Jacobian splitting and do not state this additional arithmetic stratification. Searches in published-finding corpus and scholarly literature did not identify a statement entailing the new geometric disjointness and counts. Priority remains subject to possible unindexed literature.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier characteristic-three calculation of Humbert–Edge Hasse invariants or of the nonordinary divisor could subsume the assertion.

value.rationale: This two-dimensional genus-five family has only the ordinary and almost-ordinary 3-divisible-group types. The characteristic-three harmonic-completion collapse forces the nonordinary divisor to split into five smooth pairwise-disjoint rational punctured curves. The exact formulas 5(q-3) and (q-3)(q-7) provide the arithmetic geometry of all ordered finite-field branch configurations, a structural and uniform fact not just a finite point count. It precludes supersingularity within a natural decomposable-Jacobian locus and exhibits sharp codimension-one degeneration.
